review.material: The complete public Cambridge publisher abstract was read.
review.limitations: The 21-page paper’s individual pilot studies, fabrication details and evaluation criteria were not available for close reading.

evidence.description: Primary abstract distinguishes initial pilot work from long-term objectives.

sections.title: What it is about
sections.text: Knight and Sass investigate visually expressive, customizable building assemblies. Shape grammars develop the visual language; digital fabrication develops physical components that can interlock and be assembled by hand.

sections.title: Premise
sections.text: Can housing assemblies incorporate culturally meaningful decorative variation while also addressing material and structural requirements? The abstract motivates affordability and local relevance as research goals.

sections.title: Method reported
sections.text: This paper reports a first phase of pilot studies for prototype systems using vernacular visual languages. The longer-term ambition is visual–physical grammars that generate complete CAD/CAM information for full-scale fabrication.

sections.title: Reported outcome
sections.text: The authors report promising prototypes and multiple strategies for incorporating visual properties in structural systems. The public abstract supplies no shared cost measure, structural test protocol or occupied-housing evaluation.

sections.title: Claims to keep separate
sections.text: Low-cost housing and post-disaster applications are intended benefits if the research succeeds, not demonstrated population-level outcomes in this abstract. The individual prototypes require the full paper to assess.

sections.title: What to look for in the paper
sections.text: Trace how a decorative rule affects component geometry, assembly and fabrication. Ask which constraints were tested physically and which remain future objectives.

terms.meaning: Rules connecting visual design variation with physical assembly and fabrication requirements.
Producing variations for differing requirements within a coordinated production system.
